# Components

Source: https://openui.dev/docs/components

# Components

OpenUI components are source files, not a runtime library. Each one:

- uses only framework primitives and Tailwind CSS utilities;
- has **no OpenUI runtime dependency** and no third-party runtime dependency;
- ships a plain class-joining helper instead of `clsx` or `tailwind-merge`
  (variants are disjoint, so class conflicts do not arise);
- forwards every native attribute to the underlying element.

The beta ships nine components, each implemented natively for React, Svelte,
Astro, and Vue: `button`, `input`, `textarea`, `select`, `checkbox`, `radio`,
`label`, `field`, and `theme`.

## Button

### Props

| Prop        | Type                                                         | Default   | Description                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `variant`   | `primary \| secondary \| outline \| ghost \| danger \| link` | `primary` | Visual emphasis.                       |
| `size`      | `sm \| md \| lg \| icon`                                     | `md`      | Control height and horizontal padding. |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean`                                                    | `false`   | Stretch to the container width.        |
| `type`      | `button \| submit \| reset`                                  | `button`  | Native button type.                    |
| `disabled`  | `boolean`                                                    | `false`   | Native disabled state.                 |

Every other native attribute (`aria-*`, `onClick`, `form`, …) is forwarded to
the underlying `<button>`.

### Variants

| Variant     | Use                                             |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `primary`   | The single highest-emphasis action on a screen. |
| `secondary` | Supporting action on a subtle surface.          |
| `outline`   | Bordered action in dense or neutral layouts.    |
| `ghost`     | Borderless action in toolbars.                  |
| `danger`    | Destructive or irreversible action.             |
| `link`      | Inline action styled like a link.               |

### Sizes

`sm` is 32px tall, `md` is 40px, `lg` is 48px, and `icon` is a 40×40 square.

### Accessibility

- Uses a real `<button>` element, so keyboard and screen-reader behavior is
  native.
- Includes a visible `focus-visible` ring with offset.
- Disabled buttons use both `disabled` and `pointer-events-none` plus reduced
  opacity.
- `type` defaults to `button` to avoid accidental form submission.
- For icon-only buttons, pass an accessible name:

```tsx
<Button size="icon" aria-label="Close dialog">
  <CloseIcon aria-hidden="true" />
</Button>
```

## Form controls

`input`, `textarea`, `select`, `checkbox`, and `radio` wrap their native
elements, so browser behavior and accessibility stay intact. They share one
field treatment: a 40px control height (`h-10`), a `zinc` border, a focus ring
with offset, and a red border in the invalid state.

### Shared props

| Prop      | Type      | Default | Description                                               |
| --------- | --------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds an error treatment and, where valid, `aria-invalid`. |

Native attributes (`value`, `defaultValue`, `name`, `disabled`, `required`,
`placeholder`, `onChange`, …) are forwarded unchanged.

### Input

A native `<input>` with the shared field treatment. `type` is not set, so the
browser default (text) applies and any explicit `type` still works.

```tsx
<Input type="email" name="email" placeholder="you@example.com" required />
<Input invalid aria-describedby="email-error" />
```

### Textarea

A native `<textarea>` with `rows` defaulting to `4` and a minimum height.

| Extra prop | Type     | Default | Description                 |
| ---------- | -------- | ------- | --------------------------- |
| `rows`     | `number` | `4`     | Initial visible line count. |

```tsx
<Textarea name="bio" rows={6} placeholder="Tell us about yourself" />
```

### Select

A native `<select>` with `appearance-none` and a decorative chevron. Pass
`<option>` elements as children; the component positions the chevron for you.

```tsx
<Select name="role" defaultValue="dev">
  <option value="dev">Developer</option>
  <option value="ops">Operations</option>
</Select>
```

### Checkbox and Radio

Native `<input type="checkbox">` and `<input type="radio">` styled with Tailwind
accents. Group radios by giving them the same `name`. Both accept an `invalid`
prop that adds an error outline — Radio uses a `data-invalid` attribute rather
than `aria-invalid`, because `aria-invalid` is not valid on `role="radio"`.

```tsx
<Checkbox name="terms" value="accepted" />
<Radio name="plan" value="pro" />
<Radio name="plan" value="team" />
```

### Label

A native `<label>` with form typography. Associate it with a control with
`htmlFor` (React) / `for` (Svelte, Astro, Vue), or wrap the control directly.

```tsx
<Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
```

## Field

`Field` composes a label, a control, and an optional hint or error message, and
computes the wiring a control needs: a generated `id`, `aria-describedby` for
the hint and error text, and `aria-invalid` when there is an error.

| Prop    | Type     | Default   | Description                                  |
| ------- | -------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `label` | `string` | `""`      | Visible label text.                          |
| `hint`  | `string` | `""`      | Helper text, linked with `aria-describedby`. |
| `error` | `string` | `""`      | Error text; also marks the control invalid.  |
| `id`    | `string` | generated | Control id. Generated when omitted.          |

The component hands the wiring to the control as a **`controlProps`** object.
Spread it onto any control so the control and the messages stay linked:

```tsx
<Field label="Email" hint="We never share it." error={message}>
  {({ controlProps }) => <Input type="email" {...controlProps} />}
</Field>
```

```svelte
<Field label="Email" hint="We never share it." error={message}>
  {#snippet control({ controlProps })}
    <Input type="email" {...controlProps} />
  {/snippet}
</Field>
```

```vue
<Field label="Email" hint="We never share it." :error="message">
  <template #default="{ controlProps }">
    <Input type="email" v-bind="controlProps" />
  </template>
</Field>
```

In Astro, render the control inside the default slot and pass the same `id` and
`aria-describedby` you give the Field. The component also exposes
`data-control-id`, `data-described-by`, and `data-invalid` on its wrapper:

```astro
<Field label="Email" id="email" hint="We never share it." error={message}>
  <Input id="email" type="email" aria-describedby={message ? "email-error" : "email-hint"} />
</Field>
```

## Theme

`Theme` ships the state behind dark mode plus a ready-made toggle. It has two
parts you install together:

- `theme` — a small module (`theme.ts`) with the state API and a no-flash init
  script.
- `theme-toggle` — a native icon button that cycles **light → dark → system**.

The theme is a single value, stored under the `openui-theme` key and defaulting
to `system`. The resolved theme is applied as a `dark` class on `<html>`, which
is what Tailwind's `dark:` variant targets.

| Export                | Type                            | Description                                       |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `readTheme()`         | `"light" \| "dark" \| "system"` | Reads the stored value, falling back to `system`. |
| `applyTheme(theme)`   | `void`                          | Applies the theme to `<html>` and persists it.    |
| `resolveTheme(theme)` | `"light" \| "dark"`             | Resolves `system` against `prefers-color-scheme`. |
| `initTheme()`         | `() => void`                    | Applies the stored theme and follows OS changes.  |
| `THEME_INIT_SCRIPT`   | `string`                        | Inline script for `<head>`; prevents a flash.     |

Add the init script to `<head>` so the stored theme applies before first paint,
call `initTheme()` once, and drop in the toggle:

```tsx
// app entry
import { initTheme } from "@/components/ui/theme";
initTheme();

// <head> — prevents a flash of the wrong theme
<script dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: THEME_INIT_SCRIPT }} />;

// anywhere
<ThemeToggle />;
```

Framework notes:

- **React** — also exports `useTheme()` and a `ThemeInitScript` component.
- **Svelte** — call `initTheme()` in your root layout, then use `<ThemeToggle />`.
- **Astro** — the component carries its own scoped client script; add
  `<script is:inline set:html={THEME_INIT_SCRIPT}></script>` in `<head>`.
- **Vue** — call `initTheme()` in `main.ts`, then register `<ThemeToggle />`.

Tailwind CSS v4 needs the variant declared once in your stylesheet:

```css
@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));
```

## Usage by framework

### React

```tsx
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
import { Input } from "@/components/ui/input";
import { Field } from "@/components/ui/field";

<Button variant="danger" size="lg" onClick={remove}>
  Delete project
</Button>;

<Field label="Email" error={message}>
  {({ controlProps }) => <Input type="email" {...controlProps} />}
</Field>;
```

Import paths follow your `openui.json` aliases. The default `{ui}` alias is
`@/components/ui` for React.

### Svelte

```svelte
<script>
  import Button from "$lib/components/ui/button.svelte";
  import Input from "$lib/components/ui/input.svelte";
</script>

<Button variant="outline" size="sm" onclick={save}>Save</Button>
<Input type="email" name="email" invalid={hasError} />
```

Svelte content is passed as a snippet:

```svelte
<Button>
  {#snippet children()}
    <span>Save</span>
  {/snippet}
</Button>
```

### Astro

```astro
---
import Button from "../components/ui/button.astro";
import Input from "../components/ui/input.astro";
---

<Button variant="secondary" type="submit">Save</Button>
<Input type="email" name="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
```

Astro content goes into the default slot.

### Vue

```vue
<script setup>
import Button from "@/components/ui/button.vue";
import Input from "@/components/ui/input.vue";
</script>

<template>
  <Button variant="ghost" @click="close">Close</Button>
  <Input type="email" name="email" invalid />
</template>
```

Vue content goes into the default slot.

## Customizing

Components live in your project after installation. Edit them directly. Use
`openui diff button` to see what changed before pulling a registry update, and
`openui add button --overwrite` only when you intend to replace local edits.

Add new variants or sizes by editing the component's class maps. Keep variants
disjoint — for example, do not give two variants background utilities that can
conflict — so the simple join helper remains correct.
